newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil slips on cargo deals, bearish feeling.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil slips on cargo deals, bearish feeling.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil prices slipped on Thursday on the back of an aggressively priced cargo deal and amid general product weakness, traders said.
An Irish utility bought 25,000 tonnes of high sulphur cracked for May delivery from a French major at a price heard to be $80 cif.
The deal followed a late Wednesday cracked trade from Scandinavia to a major at $82 cif, in a combination cargo along with over 10,000 tonnes of VGO.
The business pushed numbers down $3-$4 to $79/$80 cif but a later trader requirement for a cargo to fill a commitment to the same utility at end-April saw bids around $81 cif talked.
"High sulphur seemed to get a bit of an artificial boost last week and I'm happy to see numbers back nearer to what I consider reality," said one buyer.
The low sulphur market was again moribund, with cargoes talked down $1 to $88/$89 fob on a notional basis, on the back of crude's weakness, a drop in swaps and supply that far outstrips demand.
Barge values also lost some $2 in a thin buying market, with reports of good supply volumes ahead.
Refinery material traded at $84 and other grades were done at $83.50 and $83. One deal was heard done at $85 after lunch. Bunker demand was reported surprisingly quiet.
Swap prices dipped under physical values, partly on the back of the May cargo trade.

Dealers said one trading house appeared to have surplus product to shed in the ARA area and two more players would shortly be taking a cargo of around 80,000 tonnes of Venezualan product into Rotterdam.
"The supply/demand equation is not clearly mapped out for the next week," said one dealer.
